<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par74 />after the manner of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}); in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׁי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=אָבִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=15}}; in the {{GHGterm|infinitive}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=35}}; in the {{GHGterm|participle}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=19|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=39|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, all in {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֵבִי}}, always before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, hence perhaps only a scribal error).

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|l}}
5. In the ''jussive, imperfect consecutive'', and {{GHGterm|imperative Hiphʿîl}} a number of cases occur with ''î'' in the final syllable; cf. {{GHGheb|text=יַשִּׁא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=14}} (in the parallel passages {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשִּׁיא}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=2}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽחֲטִא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=11}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=22|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּתְבִּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוֹצִא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=43|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הוֹצִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=8}} (in both cases before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}). If the tradition be correct (which at least in the defectively written forms appears very doubtful) the retention of the ''î'' is to be attributed to the open syllable; while in the closed syllable of the 3rd ''sing. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}}, and the 2nd ''sing. masc.'' after {{GHGheb|text=ו}} {{GHGterm|consecutive}}, the ''î'' is always reduced to ''ē''. In the examples before {{GHGheb|text=ע}} considerations of euphony may also have had some influence (cf. {{GHGpar|75|hh}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=3}}, Baer reads with the Western school {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֵיא}}, while the Orientals read in the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=ויבוא}}, and in the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֵא}}.

On the transition of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} to forms of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} see {{GHGpar|75|nn}}.<section end=par74 />

<section begin=par75 />{{GHGpar-heading|75|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}} to reveal. Paradigm P}}

Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 149 ff.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 618 ff.—G. R. Berry, ‘Original Waw in {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} verbs’ in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|AJSL.|American Journal of Semitic Languages.}}}} xx. 256 f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|a}}
These verbs, like the verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}} ({{GHGpar|69|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|70|nosign=1}}), belong to two different classes, viz. those originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}} and those originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}},<ref>According to Wellheusen, ‘''Ueber einige Arten schwacher Verbs''‘ in his ''Skizzen'', vi. p. 255 ff., the {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} verbs, apart from some true {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}} and some probable {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}}, are to be regarded as originally biliteral. To compensate for their arrested development they lengthened the vowel after the 2nd radical, as the {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} verbs did after the 1st radical. But although there is much to be said for this view, it fails to explain pausal forms like {{GHGheb|text=חָסָ֫יָה}} (see u). It seems impossible that these should all be ''late'' formations.</ref> which in Arabic, and even more in Ethiopic, are still clearly distinguished. In Hebrew, instead of the original {{GHGheb|text=ו}} or {{GHGheb|text=י}} at the end of the word, a {{GHGheb|text=ה}} always appears (except in the ''ptcp. pass. Qal'') as a purely orthographic indication of a final vowel ({{GHGpar|23|k}}); hence both classes are called {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=גָּלַי|translate=he has revealed}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵו|translate=he has rested}}. By far the greater number of these verbs are, however, treated as originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״י}}; only isolated forms occur of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|b}}
{{GHGheb|text=שָׁלָה|translate=to be at rest}} may be recognized as originally {{GHGheb|text=ל״ו}}, in the forms in which the {{GHGterm|Wāw}} appears as a strong consonant, cf. 1st ''sing. perfect Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלַ֫וְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=26}}, the {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלֵו}} and the derivative {{GHGheb|text=שַׁלְוָה|translate=rest}}; on the other hand the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלָ֫יוּ}}. (with {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}). In {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} (Arab. {{GHGheb|text=עני}}) ''to answer'', and {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}} (Arab. {{GHGheb|text=ענו}})<ref>In the Mêšaʿ inscription, line 5, {{GHGheb|text=ויענו|translate=and he oppressed}} occurs as 3rd ''sing. masc. imperfect Piʿēl'', and in line 6, {{GHGheb|text=אענו|translate=I will oppress}} as 1st ''sing.''</ref> ''to be afflicted'', are to be seen two verbs originally distinct, which have been assimilated in Hebrew (see the Lexicon, s. v. {{GHGheb|text=עָנָה}}).<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
